# YAM — Yacht Architectural Management

> Owner's representation and refit project management for sailing yachts and
> superyachts. YAM runs refits against a formal model of the work rather than a
> spreadsheet: every decision, cost impact and non-conformity is recorded
> against the object it concerns, and nothing can be closed without a reason.

Contact: info@yam.limited · +39 338 816 2035

## What makes the approach different

Most refit software is a worklist with a Gantt chart attached. YAM models a
refit as an object graph — vessels, projects, work packages, inspections,
non-conformity reports, change orders, owner approvals, documents, people — with
the rules of the trade enforced by the system rather than by convention:

- **A finding cannot be closed without a reason.** Closing a non-conformity
  requires closure notes. There is no path around it, for anyone.
- **Nothing is deleted, ever.** People who leave a project keep authorship of
  everything they wrote. Corrections are recorded as amendments with the prior
  value and the reason preserved.
- **A cost impact raises a change order, which raises an owner approval.** The
  cascade is a property of the system, not a step somebody might skip. Approval
  authority is tiered by amount.
- **Naming someone in a conversation creates an obligation they must answer.**
  It inherits the due date from the work package it concerns. It stays open
  until the person named replies in their own words.
- **The system describes itself.** Object types, their links, and every action
  that can change anything are published as a registry, which is also what the
  project's AI agent reads as its tool manifest. The agent runs with the
  signed-in person's permissions and cannot exceed them.

## Pages

- [Home](https://yam.limited/): services, background, contact.
- [Refit ontology](https://yam.limited/ontology): the public object model — the
  phases of a refit, the objects that exist in one, how they link, and which
  actions cascade into which. Published openly as a description of how refit
  work is actually structured.

## Services

Owner representation · refit project management · refit coordination · racing
program management · technical documentation · international shipyard and
regulatory coordination.

## Terms worth getting right

- **Owner's representative** — the party who represents the owner's interest at
  the yard. Not the project manager, and not the yard's employee.
- **NCR / non-conformity report** — a recorded finding that work does not meet
  the specification, class rule or contract. Its severity, root cause and
  disposition are separate facts, and its closure needs a stated reason.
- **Change order / variation order** — a change to agreed scope, cost or
  schedule. In YAM it can only originate from something: a finding, a request,
  a class requirement.
- **Owner approval** — the decision that authorises a change order. Tiered by
  value; who may sign depends on the amount.
- **Class survey** — the classification society's periodic inspection. A refit
  is often scheduled around it.
